name: Immune-mediated Acquired Neuromuscular Junction Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Immune-mediated Neuromuscular Junction Disorders

criteria.description: Presence of fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness with fatigability
Detection of pathogenic autoantibodies against neuromuscular junction components (e.g., acetylcholine receptor, MuSK)
Electrophysiological studies showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation or increased jitter on single-fiber electromyography
Clinical improvement with immunosuppressive therapy or acetylcholinesterase inhibitors

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fluctuating muscle weakness plus either autoantibody detection or electrophysiological evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of congenital and other neuromuscular junction disorders.

searchTerms: weak muscles that come and go

blurred vision due to weak eye muscles
seeing double because eyes don't move well

trouble swallowing due to muscle problems
weak throat muscles causing swallowing issues

common.symptomName: Limb Muscle Weakness Worsening with Activity
searchTerms: arm and leg weakness worsens with use
limb weakness that gets worse with exercise

common.symptomName: Respiratory Muscle Weakness Leading to Dyspnea
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to weak breathing muscles
trouble breathing because chest muscles are weak
jaw muscle weakness that worsens with use
difficulty chewing due to muscle fatigue

occasional.notes: Less common but reported in some cases
searchTerms: dry mouth and other autonomic symptoms

imaging: Chest CT or MRI showing thymic hyperplasia or thymoma
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations; primarily autoimmune etiology
other: Electrophysiological studies demonstrating decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations affecting neuromuscular junction proteins
Proximal muscle weakness improving with activity
Presence of voltage-gated calcium channel antibodies

redFlags: Rapid progression of respiratory muscle weakness
Sudden onset of bulbar dysfunction with aspiration risk
